text:
Anya: Quick sync — we need a short decision on sprint scope for Dedicated capacity. Two asks on the table: 1) make 'soft-headroom' configurable per-pool (customer facing knob), 2) tighten the autoscale fallback so heavy bursts degrade to quantized cheaper instances before preempting. TL;DR: which do we prioritize this sprint?
Lucas: +1 for soft-headroom config. It's small infra change and unlocks customer SLAs.
Sara: autoscale fallback is more infra-risky — it touches routing and KV cache migration. Will need a canary path and rollback.
Devin: Customer ask from BrightCard — they need guaranteed 2x burst headroom for Black Friday test. They'd pay for reserved bump. If we ship soft-headroom as a knob, sales can close.
Rami: From SEs: soft-headroom alone won't help if quota accounting still drains tenants during spillover. We need quota visibility per-tenant in UI (simple graph) so customers can self-diagnose.
Anya: Good point. Proposal: M1 (must): soft-headroom knob + API flag + billing tag. M2 (nice): per-tenant quota graph in Console. M3: autoscale fallback to quantized variants. Thoughts?
Lucas: Implementation notes: soft-headroom is largely config and admission-change. We can add pool config: {\n  "soft_headroom_percent": 20,\n  "soft_headroom_mode": "elastic|strict"\n} in YAML, with Runtime reading it at pool start.
Sara: For autoscale fallback we need: routing policy that prefers cheaper quantized model family, a 200ms probe, and KV cache hotkey warming. Risk: model mismatch on output quality. Need eval guardrails.
Devin: From GTM — prioritize M1 and M2 for customer-facing wins. M3 can be experimental. Customers care about visibility + contractual headroom.
Anya: Launch criteria suggestion for M1: \n- API flag present and documented\n- Billing delta report per-customer for one week\n- E2E deploy to staging -> canary -> prod with no regressions on p95 latency\n- Product docs + sample curl/SDK snippet\nIf we agree I can write a short PRD tonight.
Lucas: Engineering acceptance checklist: \n- config schema bump and migration path\n- unit tests + admission tests\n- e2e smoke: create pool, set soft_headroom, simulate surge, ensure admission favors reserved buffer\n- perf test: token throughput with soft_headroom on vs off\nMake the migration non-breaking; default 0%.
Rami: Console UX checklist for M2 (basic): \n- small widget under pool detail showing "Quota window" with sparkline\n- hover shows last 24h peak and headroom used\n- export CSV for billing reconciliation\nWe can ship MVP with mock data if backend isn't ready — but prefer live.
Sara: Ops concerns: if soft-headroom is abused we need an alerting rule: "pool headroom consumption > 80% for > 10m" -> page. Also automated rollback if preemption spikes.
Anya: Good. Can we quantify expected engineering effort? Ballpark?
Lucas: M1: 3 dev-weeks (1 backend, 1 runtime, 1 QA/infra), M2: 2 dev-weeks (1 frontend, 1 backend), M3: 6+ dev-weeks (research + rollout).
Devin: Customer priority ordering: BrightCard wants M1 this month; another pilot (MedFlow) says M2 is critical for compliance reporting. Both willing to sign pilot contracts.
Anya: Tradeoff discussion: ship M1 + light M2 (console widget read-only) this sprint, backlog M3 for next cycle. That gives sales leverage and avoids major infra changes.
Lucas: Agree. We should add canary metric: "headroom-request-to-admit ratio" and ensure < 5% failures in canary.
Sara: Add chaos test: simulate node drain while soft_headroom active and ensure no KV corruption / stalls. I can write the test.
Anya: I'll draft the PRD with M1 acceptance, minimal M2 scope, and M3 research plan. Action items:
- Anya: PRD + acceptance criteria (today EOD)
- Lucas: start schema PR and small migration plan (tomorrow)
- Sara: chaos/rollback test plan + pre-req infra alerts (tomorrow)
- Rami: Console mockups for widget (Friday)
- Devin: confirm BrightCard pilot contract language and commit date (today)
ops-bot: Deploy pipeline triggered for branch feature/soft-headroom-schema — build queued.
Devin: One more ask — billing team needs a tag so we can show reserved-bump usage in invoices. Add billing_tag to schema.
Lucas: will include billing_tag in schema. Example config snippet in runtime: \n```yaml\npool_name: "reserved-west-1"\nsoft_headroom_percent: 25\nsoft_headroom_mode: "elastic"\nbilling_tag: "pilot_brightcard_2026-11"\n```\nSara: Note on metrics: emit "pool.soft_headroom_used", "pool.effective_capacity", and "pool.preemptions". Hook to Console dashboards.
Anya: OK final call — M1 + light M2 this sprint. We will document rollback steps and target canary tomorrow. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Lucas: +1
Sara: +1
Rami: +1
Devin: :rocket:
